original_question: What microscopic mechanism determines the collective mass along a large-amplitude collective path, in particular how do pairing correlations, repeated level crossings near the Fermi surface, nucleon-pair hopping, and smooth changes of single-particle wave functions combine to set the inertia against changing the collective coordinate?
target_in_paper: “What is the microscopic mechanism that determines the collective mass? … To deepen our understanding of the collective mass of LACM, it is desirable to make a comprehensive analysis of the microscopic mechanism determining it. A systematic comparison between the hopping mass and other collective masses discussed above will certainly serve for this purpose.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the central open problem of section 6.3—namely, elucidating the microscopic mechanisms that determine the collective mass (inertia) along a large‐amplitude collective path—and it mentions the key ingredients highlighted in the paper: pairing correlations, successive single-particle level crossings near the Fermi surface, the nucleon-pair hopping mechanism (“hopping mass”), and smooth changes of single-particle wavefunctions.
missing_details: Specify the framework: the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) method within the TDHFB theory for large-amplitude collective motion
Define the collective coordinate q(t), its conjugate momentum p(t), and the collective Hamiltonian H(q,p,n)=V(q)+½ B(q)p²+λ(q)n with B(q) the inverse inertial function
Clarify that the collective mass M(q)=1/B(q) is a local function of q along the collective path
Mention the need for a comprehensive analysis comparing the hopping mass with other microscopically calculated masses (cranking, GCM-GOA, ATDHFB, ASCC)
Quantify that the question refers to an infinitesimal change δq of the collective coordinate at each point along the path
refined_question: In the adiabatic self-consistent collective coordinate (ASCC) framework for large-amplitude collective motion in superfluid nuclei, one extracts a collective path parameterized by a coordinate q with conjugate momentum p, and derives a collective Hamiltonian H(q,p,n)=V(q)+½ B(q)p²+λ(q)n, where B(q) is the inverse inertial function (collective mass M(q)=1/B(q)). What are the microscopic mechanisms that determine M(q) at each point along the collective path? In particular, how do (i) the strength of pairing correlations, (ii) successive single-particle level crossings at the Fermi surface, (iii) the Barranco et al. nucleon-pair hopping mechanism (the “hopping mass”), and (iv) smooth adiabatic rearrangements of single-particle wavefunctions each contribute to, and combine in, setting the inertia against an infinitesimal change δq in the collective coordinate?
justification: We identified the exact open problem formulation in section 6.3 of the paper (page 10–11) and its context defining the collective Hamiltonian in section 5.2 (page 8). The draft question correctly lists the key physical ingredients but omits the definitions of the collective coordinate, collective Hamiltonian, and the requirement for systematic comparison among different microscopic mass calculations. The refined question supplies these missing details in a self-contained manner while faithfully reflecting the paper’s scope.
